background_rationale: Spent nearly three decades at Disney moving from finance and strategy roles into theme-park and resort operations, running Disneyland, Walt Disney World and then the full Experiences segment before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: On taking over from Bob Iger at Disney's annual meeting on March 18, 2026, D'Amaro said "The most important part of Disney will always be the people."

In his fiscal Q3 2026 shareholder letter, Disney raised planned share repurchases to at least $9 billion for fiscal 2026 and said Consumer Products would move from the Experiences segment to Entertainment from fiscal 2027.
In the same letter he described Disney's use of AI as primarily a way to enhance a creative process he called human-centered, artist-driven and creator-led, rather than simply a tool for efficiency.
Created a new Chief Technology Officer role reporting to him and named Karandeep Anand to it, effective Oct. 2, 2026.

personal_story.hook: A former sculpture student who joined Disneyland in 1998 now runs The Walt Disney Company.
personal_story.summary: D'Amaro grew up in Medfield, Massachusetts, and attended Medfield High School. He began college studying sculpture at Skidmore College before transferring to Georgetown University, where he earned a business administration degree in 1993. After a stint in finance at Gillette in Boston, he joined Disney at the Disneyland Resort in 1998 and spent the next decades in finance, strategy, marketing and park operations, eventually running Disneyland, Walt Disney World and the company's parks, cruise and consumer products businesses. He succeeded Bob Iger as CEO in March 2026, crediting Iger's mentorship.
